articles.title: Médicos sem registro de especialista lideram infrações em Sergipe | G1
articles.standfirst: Anúncio em redes sociais sem a prática de residência ou comprovação é infração ética, de acordo com Cremese.
articles.summary: Médicos sem registro de especialista cometem infração ética ao anunciar títulos em redes sociais, alerta o Cremese sobre áreas como psiquiatria e emagrecimento.
articles.body:
A busca por tratamentos médicos por meio das redes sociais é uma prática comum, mas que exige atenção dos pacientes. Sobre esse tema, o coordenador da Comissão de Divulgação de Assuntos Médicos do Conselho Regional de Medicina de Sergipe (Cremese), Renê Vasconcelos, afirmou, em entrevista ao Bom Dia Sergipe, nesta quinta-feira (8), que a maior parte das denúncias de infrações éticas cometidas por médicos é se intitular especialista sem ter o devido registro.

O Conselho Federal de Medicina (CFM) proíbe que médicos façam anúncios de especialidades sem possuir o Registro de Qualificação de Especialista (RQE) devidamente cadastrado no Conselho Regional de Medicina (CRM).

Segundo as normas vigentes, a conclusão de cursos livres ou de pós-graduações lato sensu não confere o título de especialista ao profissional. Apresentar-se como especialista sem o devido registro no conselho regional caracteriza infração ética.

"O maior número de infrações, com certeza, é se intitular especialista sem ser, principalmente psiquiatria, emagrecimento, área de atuação que não existe, medicina do canabinoide, que embora tenham várias pós-graduações, mas não existe essa área de atuação. Então assim, a campeã de audiência realmente é se intitular especialista sem ser", declarou Renê Vasconcelos durante a entrevista.

articles.title: Duas mulheres ficam feridas após moto bater na traseira de ônibus na Grande São Luís | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítimas foram socorridas pelo Samu. Segundo os socorristas, elas apresentavam dores na cabeça e na região pélvica, além de sinais de possível embriaguez.
articles.summary: Vítimas foram socorridas pelo Samu. Segundo os socorristas, elas apresentavam dores na cabeça e na região pélvica, além de sinais de possível embriaguez.
articles.body:
Duas mulheres ficam feridas após moto bater na traseira de ônibus na Grande São Luís — Foto: Reprodução/TV Mirante

Duas mulheres ficaram feridas após a moto em que estavam bater na traseira de um ônibus, na manhã desta quinta-feira (8), na MA-201, conhecida como Estrada de Ribamar, na região do Tambaú, na Grande São Luís .

As vítimas foram socorridas por equipes do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu), que prestaram os primeiros atendimentos no local do acidente.

Segundo os socorristas, uma das mulheres apresentava dores na região pélvica, enquanto a outra reclamava de dores na cabeça. A equipe também relatou que as duas apresentavam sinais de possível embriaguez.

Ainda não há informações sobre as circunstâncias do acidente nem sobre o estado de saúde atualizado das vítimas.

articles.title: Black Friday: como a comunicação digital acelera as vendas no ponto de venda | G1
articles.standfirst: Painéis de LED, totens e telas conectadas ajudam lojistas a atualizar ofertas em tempo real, organizar o fluxo de clientes e disputar atenção na data mais concorrida do varejo.
articles.summary: Painéis de LED, totens e telas conectadas ajudam lojistas a atualizar ofertas em tempo real, organizar o fluxo de clientes e disputar atenção na data mais concorrida do varejo.
articles.body:
Black Friday: como a comunicação digital acelera as vendas no ponto de venda — Foto: Divulgação/Amazoncopy

Nos dias que antecedem a Black Friday, o varejo físico enfrenta um problema que não aparece nas planilhas: excesso de estímulo. Vitrines lotadas de cartazes, corredores com placas sobrepostas, adesivos de liquidação colados por cima de campanhas anteriores. Quanto mais a loja tenta gritar, menos o consumidor escuta.

O comportamento de quem compra também muda. Em dias de pico, o cliente circula mais rápido, compara preços pelo celular enquanto anda pela loja e decide em poucos segundos se vale parar diante de uma oferta. Nesse cenário, a comunicação estática tem uma limitação estrutural: ela foi impressa dias antes e não acompanha o que está acontecendo na operação naquele momento.

É aí que a comunicação digital no ponto de venda deixa de ser um item estético e passa a ser ferramenta de operação.

A jornada do cliente dentro de uma loja tem vários pontos de decisão, e a maioria deles costuma ser mal aproveitada.

A vitrine é o primeiro. Um painel de LED com brilho suficiente para ser visto sob a luz do dia consegue parar quem passa pela calçada ou pelo corredor do shopping, algo que um cartaz impresso raramente faz numa data em que todas as lojas estão sinalizadas.

Dentro da loja, totens digitais posicionados em pontos de maior fluxo orientam o cliente sobre onde encontrar as categorias em promoção, o que reduz a dependência do atendimento para perguntas simples e libera a equipe para o que realmente converte.

E há o caixa, provavelmente o espaço mais subestimado do varejo. Praticamente todo cliente passa por ali antes de sair, e normalmente aguarda alguns minutos com a atenção disponível. Em um artigo publicado no blog da AC Display, unidade de negócios da Amazoncopy , sobre comunicação visual em supermercados, a empresa defende que esse intervalo pode ser convertido em nova oportunidade de venda: enquanto espera, o consumidor visualiza ofertas de itens próximos à fila, conhece o clube de vantagens ou descobre um serviço de entrega. O tempo de espera não diminui, mas deixa de ser um período vazio.

Talvez o ganho mais concreto da tecnologia na Black Friday esteja na velocidade.

Numa operação com sinalização impressa, alterar um preço significa criar arte, imprimir, transportar e trocar fisicamente o material em cada ponto. E, em rede com várias unidades, multiplicar esse processo. Na prática, muitas lojas acabam mantendo exposta uma informação que já não corresponde ao estoque.

Com sinalização digital gerenciada de forma centralizada, a troca acontece remotamente. Um produto que está encalhado pode ganhar destaque em minutos. Um item que esgotou sai da programação antes de gerar frustração no cliente e discussão no balcão. Uma oferta-relâmpago pode entrar no ar simultaneamente em todas as unidades.

Para o lojista, isso significa dois efeitos somados: menos custo com material promocional descartável e menos atrito no atendimento, já que a informação exposta corresponde ao que a loja realmente tem.

A AC Display trabalha ainda com uma camada de análise de público aplicada às telas. Por meio de câmeras conectadas ao sistema, a tecnologia estima características gerais de quem passa diante do display: faixa etária, gênero, tempo de permanência e indicadores de atenção ao conteúdo exibido.

A empresa é explícita quanto ao limite dessa leitura: o objetivo não é identificar pessoas, e sim analisar padrões estatísticos de audiência, em conformidade com a LGPD. Não há registro de nome, CPF ou histórico individual.

O valor prático está nos relatórios. Em vez de avaliar uma campanha apenas pela percepção da equipe, o gestor passa a ter dados sobre quais horários concentram maior fluxo, qual perfil predomina em cada período e quais conteúdos prendem mais atenção.

Numa Black Friday, essa informação ajuda a ajustar a programação ao longo do próprio dia, em vez de esperar o balanço no dia seguinte.

Há ainda um desdobramento comercial que interessa especialmente a supermercados, magazines e shopping centers: o retail media.

Uma loja com alto fluxo tem algo que poucos canais oferecem — audiência qualificada no exato momento da decisão de compra. Com uma rede de telas instalada, esses espaços podem ser comercializados junto a fornecedores e marcas parceiras, transformando a estrutura de comunicação em fonte de receita e não apenas em custo.

O erro mais comum é tratar a tecnologia de PDV como decisão de última hora. Instalação, definição de pontos, produção de conteúdo e treinamento da equipe levam tempo, e nenhuma dessas etapas se resolve bem na semana da campanha.

Com sede em Manaus, a AC Display atua com venda e locação de painéis de LED, totens interativos, videowall e soluções de mídia indoor para supermercados, farmácias, lojas de varejo, shopping centers, restaurantes, academias e eventos, além de gestão centralizada de conteúdo e análise de audiência por inteligência artificial.

Sua loja está pronta para se destacar e vender mais nesta Black Friday? Conheça as soluções da AC Display e descubra como a comunicação digital pode transformar os resultados do seu ponto de venda.

articles.title: Veja quais são as 30 cidades do Paraná sob alerta de tempestade, com risco de granizo e ventos de até 100 km/h  | G1
articles.standfirst: Instabilidade deve atingir principalmente o Oeste, Sudoeste e Centro-Sul do estado. Enquanto isso, temperaturas podem chegar a 35°C no Norte e Noroeste.
articles.summary: Instabilidade deve atingir principalmente o Oeste, Sudoeste e Centro-Sul do estado. Enquanto isso, temperaturas podem chegar a 35°C no Norte e Noroeste.
articles.body:
Trinta cidades do Paraná estão sob alerta laranja de tempestade, com risco de chuva intensa, queda de granizo e ventos de até 100 km/h. O aviso foi emitido pelo Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) e entrou em vigor às 9h desta quinta-feira (8). Confira as cidades abaixo.

Segundo o órgão, há risco de alagamentos, queda de árvores, danos em plantações e interrupção no fornecimento de energia elétrica.

Outras 229 cidades do Paraná estão sob alerta amarelo de tempestade, que indica perigo potencial. O aviso, que entrou em vigor às 8h56 desta quinta-feira (8), prevê chuva de até 50 milímetros por dia, ventos entre 40 e 60 km/h e possibilidade de granizo.

Enquanto isso, o calor ganha força no Norte e Noroeste do Paraná, com temperaturas que podem chegar a 35°C na sexta-feira.

Simepar aponta possibilidade de alta incidência de raios no Paraná — Foto: Rubens Vandresen/RPC

Confira as cidades sob alerta de tempestade

A Climatempo explica que esta quinta-feira terá um aumento da instabilidade, principalmente no oeste e no sudoeste do Paraná, devido a uma área de baixa pressão no Paraguai que ajuda a organizar as nuvens mais carregadas. Nessas áreas, há risco de temporais, com chuva moderada a forte, raios e rajadas de vento, mas com volumes baixos.

"Os maiores acumulados ficam concentrados no Centro-Sul e no Sudoeste, com 7,63 mm em Coronel Domingos Soares, 6,64 mm em Pato Branco e 5,49 mm em Francisco Beltrão. A chuva pode provocar alagamentos pontuais e transtornos localizados, principalmente onde as pancadas forem mais intensas. Enquanto isso, o calor aumenta no Norte e no Noroeste", dizem os meteorologistas.

Na sexta, o calor aumenta ainda mais no Paraná - principalmente no Norte e no Noroeste, onde as máximas podem chegar a 35°C. Ao mesmo tempo, a instabilidade ganha força no Oeste e em parte do Sudoeste, conforme a frente fria se organiza pelo Rio Grande do Sul.

"Com a possibilidade de chuva forte e temporais, aumentam os riscos de alagamentos, enxurradas e transtornos em áreas urbanas e rodovias, além de impactos provocados por rajadas de vento durante as tempestades", alerta a Climatempo.

articles.title: Anne Carson vence o Prêmio Nobel de Literatura 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Anúncio foi feito na manhã desta quinta-feira (8) pela Academia Sueca.
articles.summary: A Academia Sueca anunciou Anne Carson como a vencedora do Prêmio Nobel de Literatura 2026 nesta quinta-feira, conferindo à autora a prestigiada láurea mundial.
articles.body:
A escritora canadense Anne Carson venceu o Prêmio Nobel de Literatura 2026. O anúncio foi feito na manhã desta quinta-feira (8) pela Academia Sueca, instituição responsável pela concessão da láurea.

Segundo a Academia, Carson foi escolhida “por sua obra ousada e inventiva que, em diálogo lúdico com a tradição clássica, criou novas formas para a literatura contemporânea”.

O valor do Prêmio Nobel para 2026 foi definido em 12 milhões de coroas suecas (cerca de R$ 6 milhões).

Anne Carson ganhou o Prêmio Nobel de Literatura 2026. — Foto: Reprodução

A escritora canadense Anne Carson na 75ª edição do National Book Awards no Cipriani Wall Street em 20 de novembro de 2024, na cidade de Nova York. — Foto: DIMITRIOS KAMBOURIS / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / AFP

Anne Carson nasceu em 1950, em Toronto, no Canadá. Em 1981, publicou sua tese de doutorado em Estudos Clássicos, intitulada "Odi et Amo Ergo Sum".

Ao longo de toda a carreira, combinou a escrita de poesia com o trabalho de tradução e o ensino em diferentes universidades. A própria autora já identificou a etimologia das palavras como ponto de partida para todo o seu trabalho.

A década de 1990 marcou a publicação de uma obra frequentemente apontada como a maior de Carson: "Autobiography of Red: A Novel in Verse (1998)". O livro demonstra sua notável capacidade de atualizar a tradição literária clássica. Com um olhar preciso para os modos de falar e as experiências contemporâneas, Carson parte de fragmentos de poemas do poeta grego Estesícoro, do século VI a.C., sobre o monstro vermelho alado Gerião.

Livros escritos por Anne Carson, vencedora do Prêmio Nobel de Literatura de 2026, em exposição na livraria Waterstones em Londres. — Foto: REUTERS/Hannah McKay

Ao longo de sua obra, Carson explora, com leveza, as possibilidades da escrita, processo em que o esboço literário adquiriu particular importância para ela. Um exemplo é "Float" (2016), trabalho composto por 22 pequenos livros sobre temas diferentes, que podem ser lidos em qualquer ordem.

Outro é "Wrong Norma", de 2024, uma combinação diversa de textos com forte caráter performático, na qual Carson transita por diferentes campos artísticos e acadêmicos.

Suas colaborações com artistas visuais, coreógrafos e diretores de ópera e teatro demonstram a liberdade com que ela se relaciona com as expectativas literárias e os sistemas de regras.

A escritora canadense Anne Carson, vencedora do Prêmio Nobel de Literatura de 2026, tem oito livros publicados no Brasil. A autora, escolhida pela Academia Sueca por sua “obra ousada e inventiva”, começou a ter títulos lançados no país em 2017, com "O método Albertine".

Confira as obras de Carson disponíveis em português:

"O método Albertine" — lançado no Brasil em 2017 pela Edições Jabuticaba. A obra revisita Em busca do tempo perdido, de Marcel Proust, a partir da personagem Albertine, misturando ensaio, crítica literária, tradução e poesia.

"Autobiografia do vermelho" — lançado em 2021 pela Editora 34. Em um romance escrito em versos, Carson recria o mito de Gerião, transformando o monstro da mitologia grega em um jovem sensível e introspectivo.

"Sobre aquilo em que eu mais penso" — lançado em 2023 pela Editora 34. A coletânea reúne 11 ensaios sobre literatura, arte, história, tradução e criação, aproximando autores e temas de diferentes períodos.

"Eros, o doce-amargo" — lançado em 2022 pela Bazar do Tempo. Primeiro livro de crítica literária de Carson, investiga o desejo amoroso a partir da Grécia Antiga e de um verso da poeta Safo.

"A beleza do marido": um ensaio ficcional em 29 tangos — lançado em 2024 pela Bazar do Tempo. A autora narra o fim de um casamento em 29 partes, combinando poesia, ensaio e narrativa.

"Antigonick" — lançado em 2026 pela Bazar do Tempo. É uma tradução livre e experimental de Antígona, de Sófocles, com intervenções e elementos de humor no texto clássico.

"Falas curtas" — lançado em 2022 pela Relicário Edições. O livro reúne poemas em prosa que misturam memória, história, ficção e reflexão, em uma edição bilíngue.

"Vidro, ironia e deus" — lançado em 2026 pela Relicário Edições. A coletânea reúne poemas e um ensaio que aproximam experiências pessoais, literatura clássica e temas como amor, perda, identidade e religião.

Desde 1901, foram 123 laureados em 119 premiações. Isso porque em quatro delas, dois nomes foram anunciados como vencedores no mesmo ano. Até hoje, ninguém foi premiado mais de uma vez.

Não houve premiação em sete ocasiões: 1914, 1918, 1935, 1940, 1941, 1942 e 1943.

Busto de Alfred Nobel na Academia Sueca no dia em que o vencedor do Prêmio Nobel de Literatura de 2026 é anunciado, em Estocolmo. — Foto: REUTERS/ Tom Little

Rudyard Kipling foi o mais jovem vencedor do prêmio. Em 1907, quando foi nomeado, tinha 41 anos de idade. Já a mais velha foi Doris Lessing, que estava com 87 anos quando foi premiada em 2007.

Até hoje, 19 mulheres foram premiadas com o Nobel de Literatura, diante de dezenas de homens.

Ao longo dos mais de cem anos de premiação, duas pessoas declinaram ao Nobel: Boris Pasternak, em 1958, e Jean Paul Sartre, em 1964. Boris foi obrigado pelas autoridades de seu país a recusar o prêmio. Já Sartre, historicamente, sempre recusou todas as homenagens oficiais.

Os últimos vencedores do Prêmio Nobel de Literatura

Em 2025, o húngaro László Krasznahorkai foi o vencedor do Prêmio Nobel de Literatura . Segundo o comitê, o escritor venceu "por sua obra convincente e visionária que, em meio ao terror apocalíptico, reafirma o poder da arte."

Ele é conhecido por romances exigentes e distópicos, com tom filosófico, como "Sátántangó" e "Melancolia da resistência". O autor recebeu diversos outros prêmios de prestígio, entre eles o Man Booker International Prize em 2015 pelo conjunto da obra.

Ao longo da carreira, Krasznahorkai viveu períodos fora da Hungria: em 1987 esteve em Berlim Ocidental, e viajou pelo Leste Asiático nos anos 90. Ele também residiu em Kyoto e por um tempo em Nova Iorque. Essas experiências influenciaram bastante sua obra a partir dos anos 90.

Relembre as mulheres que já venceram a premiação

A lista inclui a laureada mais velha da premiação, a escritora Doris Lessing, que recebeu o Nobel aos 87 anos, em 2007. Com mais de 50 romances lançados, Doris morreu em 2013, aos 94 anos. Confira:

A láurea foi criada pelo químico e empresário Alfred Nobel. Inventor da dinamite em 1867, o sueco doou a maior parte de sua fortuna em testamento para a criação de prêmios de física, química, medicina, literatura e paz (o prêmio de economia foi criado anos mais tarde).

O documento dizia que os prêmios deveriam ser concedidos "àqueles que, durante o ano anterior, tenham conferido o maior benefício à humanidade".

Contudo, hoje em dia, conforme explica Juleen Zierath, membro do Instituto Karolinska - o júri do Nobel de Medicina-, essa regra não é mais tão levada à risca.

"Você pode ter feito essa descoberta em um estágio muito inicial de sua carreira de pesquisa, ou pode ter feito essa descoberta em um estágio muito avançado de sua carreira de pesquisador", ressalta a pesquisadora.

articles.title: Jacaré no Rio Pavuna: animal é flagrado em colchão na Zona Norte | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal foi flagrado por um morador na manhã desta quinta-feira (8), na Zona Norte; vídeo foi enviado para o Bom Dia Rio.
articles.summary: Um jacaré no Rio Pavuna foi filmado descansando sobre um colchão na Zona Norte do Rio nesta quinta-feira (8), chamando a atenção de moradores da região.
articles.body:
Um jacaré aproveitou o sol da manhã para descansar em um colchão às margens do Rio Pavuna, na Zona Norte do Rio, nesta quinta-feira (8).

O animal silvestre estava tranquilo, deitado no colchão e aproveitando o tempo ensolarado. A cena chamou a atenção de um morador que passava pelo local a caminho do trabalho. Diante da situação inusitada, ele decidiu registrar o momento e enviou o vídeo para o Bom Dia Rio .

Nas imagens, o jacaré aparece deitado no colchão, às margens do rio, enquanto aproveita o sol.

Apesar de a presença de um animal desse porte chamar a atenção, a orientação é que moradores não tentem capturar, alimentar ou se aproximar de jacarés.

Em caso de aparecimento, a recomendação é manter distância e acionar os órgãos ambientais responsáveis.

articles.title: Três mil brinquedos com irregularidade são apreendidos em lojas no Piauí  | G1
articles.standfirst: No total, 120 lojas foram fiscalizadas pelo Imepi em todo o Piauí.
articles.summary: No total, 120 lojas foram fiscalizadas pelo Imepi em todo o Piauí.
articles.body:
Uma operação do Instituto de Metrologia do Estado do Piauí (IMEPI) aprendeu três mil brinquedos e outros acessórios voltados para o público infantil após uma fiscalização em 120 lojas de todo o estado. A ação visa retirar do mercado produtos que ofereçam risco à saúde e à segurança de crianças, principalmente pela proximidade do "Dia das Crianças".

Os dados da Operação Criança Segura foram divulgados pelo Imepi na quarta-feira (7). À Rede Clube, o coordenador do setor de qualidade do órgão, Aquiles Neto, demonstrou a fragilidade dos produtos apreendidos, que não possuem o selo do Instituto Nacional de Metrologia, Qualidade e Tecnologia (Inmetro) ou utilizam selo falso.

"Tem alguns brinquedos que não tem o selo do Inmetro. Mas a gente encontra também os selos falsos. Ao adquirir o brinquedo da criança, tem que verificar: se tem o selo, ok! Mas se aquele brinquedo está com o preço bem abaixo, desconfie. Pode até fazer uma denúncia anônima para os canais do Imepi", explicou Aquiles.

Os objetos com irregularidades apresentam baixa qualidade, são fáceis de quebrar e podem possuir componentes tóxicos e prejudiciáveis aos pequenos .

Três mil brinquedos são apreendidos em operação do Imepi — Foto: Reprodução (Imepi)

"O brinquedo passa por vários testes no laborátorio. Ele testa todo tipo de pelagem, de toxicidade, e quando você verifica na embalagem, a proibição ou não para crianças menores de 3 anos. Vale a preocupação dos pais", detalha o coordenador.

O Imepi recebe denúncias de forma anônima através do WhatsApp (86) 99456-1921 e também pelo aplicativo Fala Consumidor.

*Eduarda Barradas, estagiária sob supervisão de Lucas Marreiros.

articles.title: Valmir de Francisquinho assume a Secretaria-Geral de Itabaiana | G1
articles.standfirst: Ex-prefeito Adailton Sousa também assumiu a Secretaria de Administração do município.
articles.summary: Valmir de Francisquinho e Adailton Sousa assumiram cargos nas secretarias de Governo e Administração de Itabaiana nesta quinta-feira (8).
articles.body:
Valmir de Francisquinho é nomeado secretário-geral de governo de Itabaiana. — Foto: Ascom/ Prefeitura de Itabaiana

Após derrota nas eleições para governo de Sergipe, Valmir de Francisquinho (Republicanos), foi nomeado secretário-geral de governo do município de Itabaiana . A cerimônia de posse ocorreu nesta quinta-feira (8).

Valmir de Francisquinho havia sido eleito prefeito de Itabaiana em 2018 e deixou o cargo para concorrer ao Executivo estadual nas eleições deste ano.

Com 100% das urnas apuradas, Fábio venceu a disputa para o governo do Estado com 727.291 votos (59,27%), enquanto Valmir obteve 459.908 votos (37,48%).

Além da nomeação de Valmir, o evento desta quinta-feira contou com a posse do também ex-prefeito de Itabaiana, Adailton Sousa, que assumiu o comando da Secretaria de Administração do município.

De acordo com o prefeito, Zequinha da Cenoura, a chegada dos dois reforça a equipe de governo com o foco no desenvolvimento de Itabaiana.“Convidei os dois para compor a gestão porque sei que eles têm muito a contribuir com o nosso trabalho e vão nos ajudar muito”, disse.

articles.summary: Interessados podem se cadastrar até 30 de outubro, presencialmente ou por e-mail. Aulas serão oferecidas nos turnos da manhã e da tarde.
articles.body:
O Serviço Social do Comércio (Sesc) está com inscrições abertas para as turmas de 2027 do SOS Vestibular , curso preparatório gratuito para quem pretende ingressar no ensino superior . Os interessados podem se inscrever até o dia 30 de outubro, presencialmente ou pela internet , em São Luís .

As inscrições presenciais são realizadas no Sesc Deodoro, no Centro da capital, das 8h às 11h e das 13h30 às 17h. Também é possível se inscrever pelo e-mail sosvestibular@ma.sesc.com.br . O curso terá turmas nos turnos matutino e vespertino.

As vagas são destinadas, prioritariamente, a trabalhadores do comércio e seus dependentes. Também podem participar estudantes que estejam concluindo o ensino médio em 2026 ou que já tenham concluído os estudos em escolas públicas ou com bolsa integral em instituições privadas.

Os candidatos também devem atender aos critérios de baixa renda do Programa de Comprometimento e Gratuidade (PCG), que considera a renda familiar por pessoa de até dois salários mínimos.

Para realizar a inscrição pela internet, o candidato deve preencher o formulário disponível no site do Sesc Maranhão e enviá-lo para sosvestibular@ma.sesc.com.br, junto com os seguintes documentos:

RG e CPF do candidato e, caso seja menor de idade, também do responsável;

Certificado de conclusão do ensino médio, histórico escolar ou declaração escolar da rede pública de ensino.

A lista dos candidatos selecionados será divulgada no dia 13 de novembro, no site do Sesc Maranhão e na portaria do Sesc Deodoro.

Os selecionados deverão realizar a matrícula presencialmente na Central de Relacionamento do Sesc Deodoro, entre os dias 16 e 30 de novembro, de segunda a sexta-feira, das 8h às 17h.

articles.title: Texas põe em xeque a força eleitoral de Trump | G1
articles.standfirst: Com popularidade em baixa, presidente faz três comícios em um mês em estado republicano, para tentar reverter vantagem democrata na disputa pelo Senado, e vê correligionários se distanciar dele na reta final da campanha.
articles.summary: Reduto tradicional dos republicanos, o Texas põe o partido em apuros nas eleições de novembro, levando o presidente Donald Trump a deslocar-se três vezes ao estado no último mês.
articles.body:
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, deixa palco de comício em San Antonio, no Texas, em 7 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Eric Gay/ AP

Reduto tradicional dos republicanos, o Texas põe o partido em apuros nas eleições de novembro , levando o presidente Donald Trump a deslocar-se três vezes ao estado no último mês para tentar salvar o candidato ao Senado, Ken Paxton.

O concorrente James Talarico está 7 pontos à frente , de acordo com a pesquisa recente do New York Times, e tem chances concretas de tornar-se o primeiro senador democrata a vencer no estado desde 1988 .

Trump cumpre a missão que vem se mostrando árdua, mas essencial para os republicanos manterem o controle do Senado. Nem o presidente parece acreditar na vitória de Paxton , que ele descreve, ao mesmo tempo, como o maior procurador-geral dos EUA e “um pé no saco” .

Com frequência, desfere críticas e insultos ao candidato apoiado por ele para derrotar o atual senador John Cornyn nas primárias republicanas.

A relação entre os dois transparece tensão. "Algumas pessoas podem não gostar do jeito que ele se veste. Eu não gosto" , declarou o presidente na convenção republicana em Dallas, referindo-se ao próprio candidato. Em uma gravação vazada, Paxton parece culpar Trump pelo mau desempenho da campanha: “É a guerra, são os preços da gasolina, é o diesel.”

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, discursa na Assembleia Geral da ONU, em 22 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: Mike Segar/Reuters

O apoio a Paxton nas primárias poderá custar caro a Trump , embora ele diga que não se arrependeu de ter endossado a sua candidatura para derrotar Cornyn. O senador caiu em desgraça por ter criticado a invasão do Capitólio por simpatizantes de Trump e se oposto à sua candidatura em 2024.

O presidente preferiu emplacar Paxton, alinhado ao MAGA, mas envolvido em escândalos que somavam fraude de valores imobiliários, infidelidade conjugal e um processo de impeachment na Câmara estadual, do qual foi absolvido pelo Senado.

A presença de Trump em comícios republicanos já não é garantia de triunfo eleitoral, embora ele peça aos simpatizantes para voltarem como se seu nome estivesse na cédula. Recentemente, postou em letras maiúsculas, em suas redes sociais: “Meus comícios estão salvando o Partido Republicano, mais uma vez!!!”

Na direção oposta, movidos pela baixa popularidade do presidente , atualmente em torno de 34%, candidatos republicanos vêm procurando distanciar-se dele na campanha na reta final para as eleições de 3 de novembro.

Um exemplo parece ser o do governador do Texas, Greg Abbott . Fiel aliado do presidente, mas com dificuldades para se reeleger, ele sequer compareceu ao comício de Trump na quarta-feira (7). A média das pesquisas do Real Clear Politics dá a Abbott apenas 1.7 ponto de vantagem sobre a candidata democrata, Gina Hinojosa.

O governador preferiu alegar conflitos de agenda para não se juntar ao presidente.

articles.title: Mum's last words to son before he went missing in Colombia
articles.summary: The mum of Anton Green, from Whalley Range, Manchester, is desperate to find her missing son.
articles.body:
The mother of a man missing in Colombia for two months has described how his last words to her were: "We will speak at the weekend".

Anton Green, brother of ex-Manchester United youth team defender Ro-Shaun Williams, has not been heard from since 6 August.

His mum, Nylva McKie-Williams, said it was "so unlike him not to be in contact with us".

Footballer Marcus Rashford, who described Anton as a "family friend", recently joined the appeal to help find the 43-year-old.

Anton, who is originally from Whalley Range in Manchester, moved to South America two-and-a-half years ago.

Nylva told BBC North West Tonight he kept in weekly contact with his family, but his calls home stopped suddenly at the beginning of August.

She said she became concerned when an earthquake struck another part of Colombia a few days after they last spoke.

Speaking about their final conversation, his mother said: "We ended the call by saying: 'We will speak at the weekend'."

"It just seems very, very strange and it's so unlike him not to be in contact with us."

Nylva reported her son missing to Greater Manchester Police on 10 August and also told the British embassy, but said she felt Anton had been "forgotten" and that the family had received little support.

She said: "Not knowing is the hard bit; where he is, what he's doing. It's just the unknown."

"I want him to be found and I would like the [British] embassy, the police, Interpol [to] make it a priority, not just another name in the missing system."

Nylva said while work was beginning to take place in Colombia, it had been slow to start.

She said the family's appeal had been taken up by a man living in the country, who had become a "rock" and a "godsend" to them.

According to Nylva, the man contacted the General Attorney's Office, which prompted movement in the case.

"We're now getting a bit of feedback as to actually what they're doing," she said.

A Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office spokesperson said: "We are supporting the family of a British man reported missing in Colombia and are in touch with local authorities."

A GMP spokesperson said: "We have been in touch with Anton's mother, and we have dedicated officers that have been deployed to maintain contact with the family and provide any updates should GMP receive such from overseas.

"We understand this is frustrating for Anton's family, and we are working to find them the answers they desperately seek."

articles.title: How can Guernsey prepare for a hotter future?
articles.summary: From food security to rising seas, experts say Guernsey must prepare for a changing climate.
articles.body:
Guernsey recently had its hottest summer on record , with temperatures peaking at 36.4°C (97.52F) on 25 June.

In August, the Jersey Met Office said this was in line with evidence that climate change was driving hotter summers and increasing the likelihood of drier conditions.

Professionals and businesses have highlighted the actions they believe are needed from Guernsey in response to climate change.

According to the People and Nature Survey , run by the island's Nature Commission in 2025, of the more than 900 respondents 44% said climate change was a significant concern - making it the second largest concern recorded in the survey, after development and land use.

Ilan Kelman, professor of disasters and health at University College London, said: "Small islands need to be particularly concerned about changes to the ocean as well as changes to the air in terms of heat and humidity.

"At the moment, rising sea levels are not particularly that much and are not very rapid - the concern is right now it is definitely accelerating and we expect to see far more over the coming decades."

In 2020, the States of Guernsey set a target of a 57% reduction on 1990 emission levels by 2030 and net zero by 2050.

Deputy Lindsay de Sausmarez, President of Policy and Resources, said the States of Guernsey was on track to meet its 2030 goal.

She said: "We have reduced our carbon emissions by more than half since 1990 -which is a sort of internationally recognised baseline level for measuring your emissions reductions against.

"When we look at that pathway to 2050, that is a really challenging thing to do - we can't quite see a pathway all the way there yet, but we think it will come because of how rapidly technology is evolving and innovating."

De Sausmarez credited the interim goal's progress on the island's energy policy, electricity strategy and waste strategy.

"When we approved the electricity strategy, for example, moving to our lower carbon pathway was £200m less expensive than continuing with status quo."

She added it was not just the responsibility of larger nations to respond to climate change.

De Sausmarez said: "The whole world is made up of groups of 64,000 odd people.

"We are autonomous, we can move fast, we can make things happen and we can lead the way."

Jock Pettitt, co-founder of The Farm Shop and The Soil Farm, speaks regularly to farmers locally and overseas who are affected by climate change.

"We're having conversations with our farmer peers in the UK and Europe and we're all facing the same challenges," he said.

"There are knock-on impacts and so for food security I think we're going to see difficulties getting the volume of food we've been used to."

Pettitt said investing in local sustainable farming could improve the island's resilience to climate change.

He said: "When we farm right, we get the environmental benefits from that, we look after the insects and the pollinators and the plants, the water system and the beaches and coastal environments we enjoy.

"The biggest way to motivate a farmer to do this, to do more tomorrow, is to buy the product so I think farmers need their product on the shelf and customers buying it and supporting that."

articles.title: Hurricane Isaias is expected to get stronger on its way to Florida, Alabama and Mississippi coasts
articles.summary: Isaias surged toward the U.S. Gulf Coast on Thursday as the first hurricane of the Atlantic season, prompting mandatory evacuations and school closures in parts of Florida.
articles.body: Isaias surged toward the U.S. Gulf Coast on Thursday as the first hurricane of the Atlantic season, prompting mandatory evacuations and school closures in parts of Florida. Isaias was forecast to intensify rapidly and bring strong winds and a life-threatening storm surge to the Florida Panhandle, southern Alabama and southern Mississippi when it makes landfall on the northern Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday. Heavy rain with the risk of flooding was possible into the weekend as far inland as the Tennessee Valley. The hurricane had maximum sustained winds around 75 mph (121 kph) and was moving east-northeast at 9 mph (15 kph) early Thursday morning, the National Hurricane Center in Miami said. It was centered about 445 miles (715 kilometers) south-southwest of the mouth of the Mississippi River. Coastal communities moved quickly to prepare. Some Gulf oil wells paused production, and at least four Florida school districts canceled classes for later in the week while Okaloosa County announced mandatory evacuations for some coastal areas. Governors in Florida and Alabama declared a state of emergency for dozens of counties. The National Weather Service told communities from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to Gulf County, Florida, to prepare for the possibility of “long-duration power outages.” The hurricane formed late in the season Isaias developed more than four months into the Atlantic hurricane season and was short by one day of tying a 121-year-old record for the area’s latest-forming hurricane. According to the National Weather Service, the record dates to 1905, when the year’s first Atlantic hurricane formed on Oct. 8. The Atlantic hurricane season has been unusually quiet this year because of a strong El Niño, which disrupts storm formation over that ocean. Storm activity has been above average in the Pacific, where Tropical Storm Simon formed Wednesday off Mexico. Isaias is expected to strike a swath of coastline that’s familiar with major hurricanes. One of the 20th century’s worst storms, Hurricane Camille, killed more than 250 people after hitting land near Waveland, Mississippi, in 1969. Hurricane Katrina in 2005 razed neighborhoods in Mississippi, flooded New Orleans and killed nearly 1,400 people. And Hurricane Michael leveled homes and buildings near Panama City, Florida, in 2018. Oil production and tourism already affected Ahead of the storm, oil and gas producers shut down a significant share of offshore production in the Gulf, which accounts for almost 15% of crude pumped annually in the U.S. As of Wednesday about 25% of the oil production in the region was temporarily halted, taking about 511,000 barrels a day off the market, according to the Marine Minerals Administration. It said eight of the Gulf’s 371 manned oil platforms were evacuated. With oil prices already high, the production cuts are steep enough to affect markets, though other Gulf hurricanes have caused larger disruptions, said Jim Burkhard, global head of crude oil market research for S&P Global Energy. More concerning, he said, is whether Isaias strikes as a powerful storm near refineries. As it moves inland, Isaias might also disrupt Saturday’s college football showdown between rivals Georgia and Alabama, a game President Donald Trump has planned to attend. In Alabama, the cities of Gulf Shores and Orange Beach issued a statement encouraging people in low-lying areas to voluntarily evacuate. Gulf Shores resident Maranie Adams gathered water and other supplies as her family moved belongings, including a hot tub motor, to higher ground. Her family planned to ride out the storm at home, roughly a half-mile from shore, sheltering indoors alongside their flock of chickens. “We’re having to get crates to bring them into the house so they don’t blow away,” Adams said. “It’s going to be noisy.” Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey issued a state of emergency for 40 counties, while Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis declared one for 25 counties in the Panhandle and Big Bend regions. The state also planned to deploy a Miami-based urban search and rescue task force. In Pensacola, electric utilities were pre-positioning crews to quickly repair any power outages. City officials provided sand for residents to fill sandbags to protect their homes against flooding. And Mayor D.C. Reeves urged people to check on older adult neighbors and others who might need help. “Obviously no need to panic at this point,” Reeves told a news conference. “This is really about preparation.”

articles.title: ‘Nature can recover’: Inside the race to rescue world’s crisis-hit wildlife
articles.summary: Spark of hope for a natural world beset by crisis, as conservation efforts succeed amid a 73 percent drop in wildlife.
articles.body:
Beneath the dense forest canopy of Uganda’s Bwindi Impenetrable National Park, a troop of gorillas is being quietly observed by a group of tourists who have each paid $800 for the privilege of the experience.

In villages around the park, a thriving economy has grown off the back of the gorillas’ presence here, from the sale of wood carvings to visitors and the provision of accommodation for up to 40,000 tourists a year.

In the national park, which sprawls along the edge of the Rift Valley and the border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), there are many local jobs for rangers and guides.

But deeper into the forest, more mountain gorillas live away from human contact, quietly enhancing the natural world around them through their daily routines of foraging, nest building and dispersing seeds.

And, crucially, by increasing their own populations.

In the 1980s, the mountain gorilla was on the fast track to extinction. Now, there are more than 1,100 living in thriving populations in Uganda, Rwanda and the DRC.

Theirs is a story of conservation success that spills beyond the species themselves, into the nature they live in, and the human communities they exist alongside.

“The mountain gorilla story shows us that conservation can work,” Tara Stoinski of the Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund tells Al Jazeera. “It’s a really important example of the effort that’s needed to make that happen – decades of sustained conservation action that includes direct protection, science-informed management and meaningful community support and involvement.”

This is welcome news for a natural world beset by crisis.

According to this year’s Living Planet Report by the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), over the past 52 years, there has been a 73 percent decline in the average size of monitored wildlife populations. Across the world, habitats have been degraded and lost as overexploitation, climate change, pollution and invasive species take their toll.

But the report also highlights important recoveries in populations of green turtles, bluefin tuna, tigers and Southern African elephants. “For too long nature has been undervalued,” says Andrew Terry, chief conservation officer at the Zoological Society of London, who helped produce the report. “But these declines are not inevitable and change is possible. Nature can recover, and these stories are a powerful reminder of this.”

The WWF says these conservation successes demonstrate how international partnerships drive results. Intergovernmental commitments from tiger range countries, including India, Bhutan, Nepal, Laos and China, helped increase global wild tiger numbers by more than 70 percent between 2010 and 2025.

In 2025, the green sea turtle became the first marine turtle ever to be downlisted from “endangered” to “least concern” on the International Union for the Conservation of Nature Red List. That reflected 50 years of species research, active protection of nesting females and eggs, measures to reduce fishing gear and sustained community engagement.

Professor Brendon Godley is a leading conservation scientist at the University of Exeter and the Sharjah Marine Research Centre in the United Arab Emirates and has spent much of his career dedicated to researching and protecting sea turtles. “Conservation success stories are hugely important because they demonstrate that declines are not inevitable,” he tells Al Jazeera.

“The recovery of species such as green turtles shows that when science, policy, enforcement and public support align, populations can rebound, sometimes remarkably so. However, they are not grounds for complacency.”

Indeed, these conservation triumphs are small battles won in an ongoing war against the degradation of nature. The WWF’s Living Planet Report highlights the three systems that are primarily driving the destruction of nature: the global food system, which is the leading cause of habitat loss as areas are cleared to grow crops; the energy system, which fuels climate change through burning fossil fuels; and the finance system, which bankrolls harmful activities, for example, large-scale infrastructure or mining projects.

Kirsten Schuijt, director general of WWF, says these industries and systems need to be transformed. “Progress is already under way,” she tells Al Jazeera. “Not everywhere, and not yet at the scale required, but enough to demonstrate that change is possible.”

The return of a species can have a powerful effect. In 2010, Atlantic bluefin tuna populations had declined by 80 percent and the species was listed as endangered. They had disappeared from much of their historical range, including UK waters. Yet today they are returning in numbers not witnessed in generations, perhaps ever.

“What makes this story particularly powerful is that the recovery is visible,” says Tom Horton, research fellow at the University of Exeter. “Coastal communities, fishers and sea-users who had never seen a bluefin tuna in British waters are now encountering them regularly. It transforms conservation from an abstract concept into something tangible.”

These successes serve as inspiration for other conservation projects in the fight against species decline, like that of the largest primate on Earth, the critically endangered Grauer’s Gorilla. Its home range lies within the vast remote forests of the DRC, living in a landscape beset by instability and habitat loss. Its numbers have dropped by an estimated 60 percent to just 6,800 today.

Urbain Ngobobo, country director for the Dian Fossey Fund in the DRC, explains that the challenge of restoring numbers there is significant but so is the opportunity.

“Every forest we help communities protect,” he says, “every gorilla we are able to monitor and every young Congolese person who develops the skills to become a conservation leader, represents progress.

“That is where hope comes from – not from assuming the future will be easy, but from knowing that our actions today can change what is possible tomorrow.”

articles.title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds
articles.summary: Retailer issues update after BBC contacted by cyber criminals who said this week's breach went beyond "basic contact details"
articles.body:
Asos has told its customers that hackers are in possession of detailed profiles of potentially millions of the online store's users.

It issued the update after BBC News told the retailer it had been contacted by cyber criminals who said this week's breach went beyond the "basic contact details" Asos previously said might have been accessed.

Names, addresses, phone numbers, emails and customer numbers are now in the hands of cyber criminals.

So too are the searches customers have made on the website. Terms like "reclaimed vintage", "glamorous wide fit" and "Asos petite" are visible in the data.

With this information, scammers may be able to craft potent phishing attack emails or phone calls.

The risk to individuals is now higher and customers are being warned about potential impersonation scams.

In its email to customers, Asos confirmed data profiles were taken but said no bank details or passwords were accessed.

"Please remain cautious of unexpected messages or calls claiming to be from Asos," it said.

"We will never ask you to share passwords, security codes or payment details through an unsolicited message or call."

The company did not respond to questions about the scale of the breach.

The high profile hack made global headlines on Tuesday when cyber criminals used Asos's own app system to send a pop up notification to potentially millions of people.

Later that day the firm confirmed to shareholders via the London Stock Exchange that the pop up was sent by an "unauthorised third party" and "basic personal information including name and contact details may have been accessed."

The company then sent an email to customers with similar wording.

On Wednesday evening the cyber criminals responsible contacted the BBC sharing a sample of the stolen data which showed the true extent of the hack.

The BBC held off publishing this article to allow Asos to contact its customers first.

Asos said it is still investigating the data breach and it would "contact customers directly where we believe additional information, support or action may be required".

The UK fashion site explained to customers that hackers gained access to an Asos employee account by "impersonating a trusted contact to obtain log in credentials".

With that log in to an unnamed service, the hackers were able to download the customer data.

In the pop up notification send to customers by the hackers, they claimed they had "compromised the Snowflake instance".

Snowflake is a popular data storage and analysis company whose customers have been breached in the past due to unauthorised log ins.

The cyber criminals, calling themselves Xuanyewen, claimed to the BBC they used a platform which is built natively on top of Snowflake - called Simon AI - to gain access to the data.

Simon AI has been contacted for comment. Snowflake previously said its platform had not been breached.

Asos said customers are not being asked to take any action.

But cyber security experts have warned users to change passwords as a precaution and be on alert for suspicious activity.

"Passwords have not been stolen, so be highly suspicious of any unsolicited text or email asking you to change or share yours," said Trevor Dearing, Senior Director of Critical Infrastructure at Illumio.

"Expect scammers to mention the attack, use your personal details to seem genuine, and create urgency, such as threatening to lock your account within 24 hours."

Asos said its website and app are safe to use and "we know our customers trust us with their information".

"We take that responsibility seriously and have already taken additional steps to further strengthen security controls," it said.

articles.title: Husband accused of Norfolk GP murder appears at Crown Court
articles.summary: Mark Cain is accused of murdering his wife Hannah Cain, who was found dead at home on Sunday.
articles.body:
The husband of a GP who was found dead at her home has appeared before a Crown Court, charged with her murder.

The body of 45-year-old Hannah Cain, known to her patients as Dr Hannah Terry, was found at a property in Fern Hill, Dersingham, Norfolk, on Sunday.

Mark Cain, 45, also of Fern Hill, was charged with murder on Tuesday.

Appearing via video link from HMP Norwich, he spoke only to confirm his name and that he understood proceedings at King's Lynn Crown Court. He was remanded in custody until a plea hearing on 3 December.

Steven Ball, prosecuting, said Mark Cain was accused of the murder of his wife on 3 October into the early hours of 4 October at their family home.

He said emergency services attended and Hannah Cain was found "unconscious and unresponsive".

A post-mortem examination recorded that she had sustained "blunt force injuries to the head" and "neck injuries consistent with compression to the neck", he said.

Mark Cain was not asked to enter a plea and no application for bail was made.

The Fern Hill address is just over a mile from Sandringham House, one of the royal residences of the King and Queen.

Dr Hannah Terry, as she was known professionally, was listed as a member of the practice team at Grimston Medical Centre.

She served in a pool of doctors who were regularly on call for members of the royal family nearby.

On Wednesday, her family described her as "kind, generous and loving".

articles.title: Gruesome injuries throw spotlight on France’s policing of high school protests
articles.summary: PARIS — The police tear gas grenade shattered the 14-year-old’s jaw and many of his teeth.
articles.body: PARIS — The police tear gas grenade shattered the 14-year-old’s jaw and many of his teeth. The officer who fired it was taken into custody a week later and charged with violent mutilation, punishable by up to 15 years in prison. Following surgery, the boy cannot speak and can only eat with a straw, his mother says. Other adolescents have also suffered life-changing injuries blamed on police weaponry during nationwide protests by high school students demanding more funding for run-down schools. In the former mining town of Lens, a 15-year-old lost a hand in an incident involving a police stun grenade. In Tours, in the wine-making Loire region, the prosecutor there says a police riot-control round is suspected in the partial blinding of a 16-year-old. Beyond physical wounds, the massive use of police arrests and tactics that government critics and human rights campaigners allege have been unnecessarily violent is giving a generation of French schoolchildren — and soon-to-be voters — a real-life education about state power and their rights as citizens, and how the two sometimes clash. “It politicizes you at an incredible speed,” said Alexis Baudelin, a Paris attorney for more than a dozen youngsters taken into custody. “For many of them — for all of them — this was one of the first times that they’d taken part in a demonstration, coming together in a public space to voice demands they considered legitimate.” Police have swept up thousands of young people According to the Interior Ministry, police have made more than 6,600 arrests — mostly of people under 18 — since protests began snowballing last week, including 488 people detained during nationwide demonstrations Tuesday. The movement demanding increased funds and more replacement teachers for schools started in a Paris-region high school in mid-September. Lawyers and researchers who study French policing caution that the muscular response could spawn disillusioned young adults soured on the Republic and its promises of “ Liberty, Equality, Fraternity. “Police have been less forgiving with teenage protesters than they previously were when farmers, a powerful lobby in France, doused government buildings with manure, blocked roads and set fires. Baudelin, the lawyer, said his young clients have had a crash course in “unrestrained violence from the police.” “Being locked up for hours and hours with nothing, in cells that are for the most part extremely unsanitary, in police stations that smell terrible, where you can’t sleep, with police officers telling you that if you don’t talk, if you don’t tell the truth, threatening you, telling you that your life is going to be ruined,” he said. “It’s an experience that can be deeply traumatic and is completely out of proportion.” Use of some police grenades suspended Amid a growing outcry, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez announced Wednesday that the model of stun grenade suspected of mutilating the teenager in Lens will no longer be used against high schoolers, in light, he said, of a “strong possibility” that such a weapon was involved in ripping off the pupil’s hand. “We need to understand exactly what happened,” Nunez said. Still, he has also defended police actions as proportionate in “almost all cases.” He says police have been obliged to intervene when protests led to rioting, vandalism and other violence, and have done so mindful that they’re largely dealing with children. “You don’t handle a high schoolers’ movement in the same way as one by adults,” the minister said to broadcaster RTL. In the case of the 14-year-old with a smashed jaw and teeth, the officer who fired his grenade launcher directly at him during a protest in Saint-Ouen l’Aumone, northwest of Paris, said during questioning in custody that he acted in “a fraction of a second” to protect a female colleague who’d exchanged blows with the boy, according to a statement from the prosecutor’s office leading the investigation. It described the officer’s actions as disproportionate, resulting in a preliminary charge against him of violence by a public official causing mutilation or permanent disability. Suspended from duty and barred from carrying a gun, he is the first officer facing potential prosecution in 18 investigations opened so far into suspected police misconduct during the protests. The boy, Eden, sent his mother a video from outside his school, showing police and some protesters, just moments before the officer shot him with the gas grenade, she said, speaking to The Associated Press and other media on condition that she not be identified to preserve the anonymity of her child. But when she then called him, it was one of his classmates who answered, screaming that her son had been hit in the face and was on the ground, bleeding with his jaw and top teeth broken and bottom teeth “completely ripped out,” she said. “It’s shameful, it’s appalling, it’s violent, it’s disgusting, it’s despicable — I could give you a whole list of words,” she said. “They are dealing with children. And children demanding what? Simply better conditions in which to study.” Teens emerge more defiant In the crowds that demonstrated in Paris on Tuesday, marching boisterously from one city square to another, AP found three Paris-region teenagers who said they were arrested, handcuffed, searched, held in custody but then released with no criminal charges last week. Samy and Warkya, both 17, said they were detained together with another friend. They believe that police picked on them because of their color. Warkya and the other friend are Black and Samy described himself as Arab. French officials have repeatedly denied that there is racism in the police ranks. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said in parliament this week that such accusations are “lies.” Samy said the officers who stopped them said, “’You, you and you, you’re coming with us.’” There was no apparent motive, because “we weren’t wearing hoodies, we had nothing on us, our faces were visible,” he said. “Here in France, they don’t listen to us. They would rather send in the police than listen to us and put measures in place to improve our daily lives,” he said. Warkya said her first experience of police custody only reinforced her determination to protest but also taught her to run when officers appear. “The police are more powerful than us,” she said. “There’s nothing we can do.”

articles.title: How much does France spend on education compared with the rest of Europe?
articles.summary: Amid student protests, Al Jazeera visualises how French spending stacks up against defence and healthcare.
articles.body:
French high school students have been protesting for more than two weeks over conditions in schools, including overcrowded classrooms and staff shortages, and they show no sign of stopping.

The unrest began on September 21 when pupils blockaded a school in the Paris suburb of Creteil, and within a week, their protest had spread across the country with students and police clashing violently.

On September 29 , the demonstrations coincided with a nationwide public sector strike, in which teachers joined other state workers against a proposed pay freeze. More than 6,100 people have since been arrested.

With the government under pressure to rein in spending as its debt rises, Al Jazeera looks at how much France invests in education, how it compares with the rest of Europe and how it measures up against what the country spends on healthcare and defence.

How much does France spend on schooling?

According to the latest data from Eurostat, the European Union’s statistics agency, France’s public spending on education amounts to 5.1 percent of its gross domestic product (GDP). That figure does not include private spending, such as school fees paid by families.

The French Ministry of National Education uses a broader measure, known as domestic expenditure on education, which counts all the money that goes into education, whether from the state, local authorities, businesses or households. As well as teaching, it covers adult and continuing training and related costs such as school meals, boarding and transport.

By this measure, France spent 199.2 billion euros ($223bn) on education in 2025, equivalent to 6.7 percent of its GDP and 2.4 billion euros more than in 2024, according to provisional ministry figures.

Spending has more than doubled since 1980, even after accounting for inflation. But the economy has grown too, so education spending’s share of GDP is lower today than it was in the mid-1990s.

Secondary education accounted for the largest share of spending at 73.7 billion euros (37 percent), followed by primary education at 60 billion euros (30 percent), higher education at 45.6 billion euros (23 percent) and adult and continuing education at 19.7 billion euros (10 percent), according to the National Education Ministry.

How much do other European countries spend on education?

Among European countries, Sweden spends the largest share of its GDP on education at 7.3 percent in 2024, followed by Iceland (7 percent) and Belgium, Estonia and Finland (6.3 percent each), according to Eurostat.

The lowest spenders are Ireland (2.7 percent), Greece (3.9 percent), Romania and Italy (4 percent each), and the United Kingdom and Spain (4.1 percent each).

At 5.1 percent, France is joint 13th, level with the Netherlands and Slovakia, and above the EU average of 4.8 percent.

But above-average spending has not shielded France from a problem affecting much of the developed world. Teacher shortages are growing across countries in the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, according to the OECD’s latest Education at a Glance report.

Rather than leaving posts empty, many countries are filling them with teachers who lack full qualifications. In the 2024-2025 school year, 9 percent of primary and secondary teachers across the OECD were not fully qualified.

In France, the strain is most visible in secondary schools. About 11 percent of secondary teachers are not fully qualified, compared with less than 3 percent in primary schools. Furthermore, lower secondary classes average 26 pupils, compared with 23 across the OECD.

That echoes what pupils have been saying during the latest protests : Classes are large, and absent teachers are not being replaced. Some also described dilapidated buildings, a shortage of tables and chairs and, in some schools, rodent infestations. The intense heatwaves that hit France this year exacerbated existing problems in neglected buildings, many of which have no air conditioning, students said.

Teachers also feel undervalued. Only 4 percent said their profession is valued in society, the lowest share of any country surveyed and far below the OECD average of 22 percent.

Historical UNESCO data showed France’s education spending slipped from 5.5 percent of GDP in 2017 to 5.3 percent in 2022 although it remained the ninth-highest among 29 European countries with data. A brief rise to 5.7 percent in 2020 reflected the pandemic shrinking the economy, not extra spending.

France was one of 14 countries where the share fell. Norway and Denmark saw the steepest drops while Slovakia, Slovenia, Lithuania and the Czech Republic recorded the biggest rises.

What else are these nations spending on?

The protests have coincided with nationwide public sector strikes over the government’s proposed 2027 budget , which seeks 54 billion euros ($61.3bn) in savings as French President Emmanuel Macron’s government tries to rein in a large public deficit.

Unions and public sector workers object in particular to a plan to freeze state employees’ salaries, which is expected to save about 2 billion euros ($2.27bn).

Across Europe, most governments spend more on education than on defence, but healthcare takes the largest share of national income of the three, according to 2022 data from the World Bank and UNESCO.

France spent 11.9 percent of its GDP on healthcare in 2022, one of the highest shares in Europe.

articles.title: Russian attack on buses in Ukraine’s Kramatorsk kills at least 30 people
articles.summary: Eighteen people were wounded in strike on the city in eastern Donetsk region, local authorities say.
articles.body:
A Russian attack on two buses has killed at least 30 people and wounded 18 others in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk, near the front line, authorities said.

The local prosecutor’s office on Thursday posted photos of bodies and debris strewn across a road in front of the burning metal shell of a bus.

Police said the attack took place on a street where two city ⁠buses were operating at the time. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described it as a bus stop.

The Donetsk governor accused Russia of “deliberately targeting civilians”.

“For them [the Russians], a bus with passengers is an attractive target precisely because one strike can kill as many people as possible,” Vadym Filashkin wrote on Telegram.

Police said the buses were hit with a glide bomb.

There was no immediate comment from Moscow on the attack. Russia denies targeting civilians, though it has regularly pounded Ukrainian cities, towns and other targets during its full-scale invasion that began in February 2022.

Kramatorsk is one of the key cities that Russia has not yet captured in Ukraine’s eastern Donetsk region, which Moscow claims as part of Russia.

It has been a logistics and supply hub for the Ukrainian military for much of Moscow’s war and is part of the so-called “fortress belt” that troops are fighting to keep hold of.

Russian forces have edged close to the city’s eastern edge, which has prompted calls for civilians who remain to relocate to safer regions of Ukraine.

Kramatorsk City Council said it was “yet another horrific crime committed by the Russian army against the civilian population”.

“Once again, the Russians have struck a location where there are absolutely no military targets,” it added.

Elsewhere in Ukraine, the death toll from Wednesday’s Russian missile attack on a residential building in the city of Pryluky in the northern Chernihiv region rose to 22 , including five children, Governor Vyacheslav Chaus said in a statement on Telegram.

President Zelenskyy said a cruise missile directly hit the building in Pryluky, about 150km (93 miles) east of the capital, Kyiv.

Meanwhile, in Russia, a drone caused a fire at a data centre belonging to Russian technology company Yandex, the firm told the AFP news agency on Thursday.

Unverified images published on social media showed columns of thick, black smoke pouring from the roof of the building, which the company said was in the central Ryazan region, southeast of Moscow.

Russia and Ukraine have intensified long-range strikes on each other in recent months, with some of the latest Russian attacks targeting Ukrainian data centres and logistics warehouses.

The former head of Ukraine’s Centre for Countering Disinformation said Kyiv was responsible for the strike on the Yandex facility, writing on Telegram: “Two can play at this game”.

The firm is Russia’s largest technology company.

Often dubbed “Russia’s Google”, Yandex runs the country’s most popular search engine, as well as a food-ordering and ride-hailing application used by tens of millions of people across the Russian-speaking world.

articles.title: Malaysia PM says will work on Myanmar’s ASEAN reintegration
articles.summary: Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing in Malaysia for a two-day visit, his first since he became president in April.
articles.body:
Malaysia’s prime minister has said his government will do “whatever possible” to ensure Myanmar’s reintegration into the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), after hosting talks with Myanmar’s military-backed President Min Aung Hlaing.

The Myanmar leader is in Malaysia for a two-day visit, his first since he became president in April, as part of a wider diplomatic push to bring the country back into the international fold after staging a 2021 coup that triggered an ongoing civil war.

“I would say that we and our part in Malaysia, will do whatever is possible to make sure that we enhance this collaboration and ultimately, take Myanmar as part of our community of nations, without prejudice, and particularly in the context of ASEAN,” Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim told a media briefing following the talks on Thursday.

Myanmar has been excluded from high-level ASEAN political meetings since 2021 over the lack of progress in implementing a peace plan proposed by the bloc.

Ibrahim also said he would continue working with Min Aung Hlaing on the repatriation of thousands of Myanmar nationals, adding that Myanmar had accepted the return of 10,493 of its nationals so far.

It is unclear if any of the returnees included minority Muslim Rohingya, who are facing persecution in Myanmar and have been denied citizenship.

Anwar added that the repatriation of Myanmar nationals would be carried out on a “voluntary, safe and dignified basis”.

Min Aung Hlaing told the news conference that Myanmar will accept more migrants held in Malaysia “as soon as possible”.

The two leaders also spoke about how to deepen cooperation across several areas, including trade, energy, security and economic matters.

Anwar has faced criticism from rights groups for repatriating migrants to Myanmar, where more than 100,000 people have been killed since 2021. He has also been accused of legitimising the presidency of Min Aung Hlaing, who was formally elected in April following a vote widely seen as illegitimate.

On Wednesday, Human Rights Watch called on Anwar to pressure Min Aung Hlaing to end human rights abuses in Myanmar and to halt what it described as plans to “forcibly return” people who had fled the country.

articles.title: Jaguar’s new electric car is a high-stakes bet on a whole new aesthetic
articles.summary: British luxury automaker Jaguar has launched its first vehicle since a radical rebrand that caused consternation, and sparked a small-time culture war with some critics calling it “woke.”
articles.body: British luxury automaker Jaguar has launched its first vehicle since a radical rebrand that caused consternation, and sparked a small-time culture war with some critics calling it “woke.” Big and broad, with no sign of Jaguar’s traditional curves, the Type 01 is a fully electric four-door grand tourer that may unsettle fans of the manufacturer’s previously heritage-heavy image. But the brand claims it is “the most technically advanced” and aerodynamic Jaguar ever engineered,” according to a press statement from parent company JLR on Wednesday. The announcement is a big step in Jaguar’s relaunch, which got off to a decidedly rocky start in 2024. Back then, under the tagline “copy nothing,” Jaguar published a promotional video featuring a diverse cast of models posing and moving through an otherworldly landscape. The video was notable for the fact that it didn’t feature any cars, and it drew the ire of traditionalists, who accused Jaguar of going “woke.” “The internet went mad, the anti-woke brigade went mad, even Elon Musk criticized it,” said automotive journalist Mark Smyth. “It threw out everything Jaguar has built over a century, including its customers.” ‘Showpiece for the elite’ The Type 01 will be available from early 2027, with prices starting from £130,000 ($172,000), moving the company firmly into the upper end of the luxury car market. Both the new model and the wider rebrand present “a massive risk” to the business, according to Smyth and other industry commentators. “Gone is the curvaceous design legacy of the brand, replaced by brutalist minimalism and cold surfaces,” Smyth added, also highlighting the car’s cutting edge technology and engineering. “This is not a mainstream production car though, it is a showpiece for the elite,” he said. “The Type 01 is probably too big for most UK cities, suggesting the US is its main target market,” said Smyth, referencing the car’s 5.2 meter (17 feet) length and two meter (6.6 feet) width. Writing in The Guardian, journalist Zoe Williams raised similar concerns, alleging that the Type 01 would be too big “to fit into any UK car parking space,” adding that the vehicle “looks more like a tank than a car.” Stuart Masson, editorial director at automotive market advisory firm The Car Expert, told CNN that the Type 01 is a gamble that could prove decisive for the survival of the company. “I think Jaguar was a brand that probably more than any other really kind of relied on its heritage and its glory days from in particular the 1950s,” he said. “The rebrand consciously basically just swept all that away in one go and said ‘we’re brand new, we’re starting again.’” “So it really upended everything that people thought about Jaguar, which was the point, but when you do that you are going to inevitably upset a lot of people who expect the company to be a certain way,” he added. “The real test,” he said, “is how they’re going to go trying to sell an electric Jaguar for more than double the price of what the old Jaguars tended to be. “If they’re going to survive they have to do something different, but this is very much last chance saloon stuff for Jaguar,” he said.

The new model's design is a marked departure from Jaguar's traditional curvaceous look.

articles.title: Photos: Protests erupt after 87-year-old evicted woman dies in Madrid
articles.summary: Nationwide outrage grows after the death of woman whose eviction sparked protests and political tensions.
articles.body:
The death of an 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her longtime Madrid home ignited nationwide outrage has intensified Spain’s debate over housing and pushed the country into a political crisis.

Maria del Carmen Abascal, known widely as “Maricarmen”, died in hospital on Wednesday, her lawyer confirmed, weeks after televised images showed police removing her on a stretcher from the flat where she had lived for seven decades. Activists said her case exposed the human cost of soaring rents and aggressive evictions.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez led tributes online, calling her “a symbol” of renters struggling with Spain’s affordability crisis and writing on X: “All my love to Maricarmen’s family and loved ones. … Rest in peace.” Protesters gathered near parliament chanted: “Maricarmen lives. The fight goes on!”

Her lawyer, Beatriz Duro, said activists were devastated, calling the eviction “shameful violence” that showed “the impact it can have on people’s health”. Housing groups stressed that although a deal was eventually reached allowing her to return home, the agreement came “too late” after a “harrowing ordeal”.

Spain’s average rent has almost doubled in a decade, and the government said more than a quarter of tenants spend about 40 percent of their income on housing and utilities – more than double the EU average.

Abascal’s removal from her home so the property could be relet at a higher price set off protests across Spain, a planned general strike next month and mounting pressure on politicians. After failing to pass emergency housing measures, Sanchez called an early election for November 29, hoping to channel public anger into support for his Socialist Party.

Conservative opposition leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo also offered condolences, urging “respect” and warning against using Abascal’s death for political gain.

articles.title: Caretaker killed and two teachers injured in knife attack at Poland school
articles.summary: Police say they foiled another school attack on Thursday, and a day after a stabbing at another Polish school.
articles.body:
A 37-year-old caretaker has died after being stabbed by a former pupil at a school in Poland, police have said.

The 15-year-old entered the primary school in Leszczydół-Nowiny, north of Warsaw, at around 09:00 (07:00 GMT) and attacked the caretaker, 37, before being overpowered by a teacher and the school's headteacher who were also injured.

Polish police said they had also detained a 17-year-old boy in another town a day earlier after he had indicated an intention to do "something spectacular" at his school.

Also on Wednesday, a 19-year-old was arrested on suspicion of a stabbing attack at another Polish school in which seven people were injured.

The 15-year-old who attacked the caretaker was carrying three knives, Poland's interior ministry spokesperson Karolina Galecka said.

The boy used to study at the primary school, but his motives for the attack are unclear, Galecka added.

Polish media report that the caretaker had tried to stop the 15-year-old from entering the school.

The teacher and the headteacher's lives are not in danger, the ministry's spokesperson said.

Before news of Thursday's stabbing in Leszczydół-Nowiny, Mazowsze Police announced it had prevented a separate school stabbing in the region.

Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the 17-year-old detained in the town of Sierpc, north-west of Warsaw, "had stated on school grounds that he planned to do something... dangerous - that he intended to harm someone".

Teachers had alerted the police, who found that the teenager was in possession of two knives.

"The young person had been searching for information on how to orchestrate a 'bloody' event of this kind," Kierwiński said.

articles.title: At least 30 people killed in Russian bus bombing in Ukraine
articles.summary: At least 30 people were killed when a Russian bomb struck two buses in the Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk, local officials said, as Moscow’s intensifies attacks.
articles.body: At least 30 people were killed when a Russian bomb struck two buses in the Ukrainian frontline city of Kramatorsk Thursday, local officials said, as Moscow’s intensifying attacks grow ever more deadly. Another 18 people were wounded when the bomb hit a street in the city at 10 a.m. local time (3 a.m. ET), Ukraine’s National Police said in a statement. Kramatorsk’s Regional Governor Vadym Filashkin accused Russia of deliberately targeting civilians, sharing images of a charred bus wreckage and bodies and body parts on the road next to it. Filashkin said he was shutting down public transport in the city and neighboring Sloviansk in light of “the sharp deterioration of the security situation.” President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a statement on X that Russia struck “an ordinary public transport stop” in Kramatorsk with an aerial bomb. In a later post, he said doctors were fighting to save the lives of those injured and “some of those killed have still not been identified because of the severity of their injuries.” Kramatorsk is close to the active frontline and part of Ukraine’s industrial Donbass region, which has been central to President Vladimir Putin war plans. Civilian casualties have surged as Russia intensifies attacks across Ukraine, and the country Ukraine runs low on air defense munitions. There has also been an uptick in daytime attacks in recent weeks, creating a round-the-clock threat to civilians. On Wednesday, a missile strike on a residential building in the north of the country killed 22 people, including five children. Moscow has repeatedly denied that it deliberately targets civilians in Ukraine.

And Christa Pike’s lawyer details her condition after her botched execution. Here’s what to know today.
